domain_label: INBDE Foundation Knowledge Material Map (Foreign-Trained Dental Graduate Pathway)
purpose: A method for turning the INBDE's Foundation Knowledge (FK) axis into a defensible study map for a foreign-trained (non-CODA) dental graduate: which biomedical-science FK areas exist as verified from the JCNDE Domain of Dentistry, what a candidate must study under each, which authoritative JCNDE/ADA artifacts define and verify them, and how to plan study honestly given that no official per-FK item weight is published and the full 56 Clinical Content enumeration was proxy-blocked — never fabricating FK numbering, weights, or the CC list the research file could not verify.
assumptions: no directly-read official JCNDE PDF was available at compile time: the Item Development Guide, Domain of Dentistry Model, and Candidate Guide all returned HTTP 403 under the session egress policy, so the FK enumeration is reconstructed from search-engine snippets of those official pages plus corroborating secondary aggregators (Penn Libraries, UOP Dugoni) and is tagged [ESTIMATE - high confidence], not [FACT]
the FK axis is only one axis of a two-axis blueprint (10 FK x 56 CC); this KB maps the FK axis and names the CC axis as a verified structural fact while flagging its full enumeration [UNKNOWN]

no official per-FK item-weight table is published by JCNDE, so study time is allocated by integrated coverage of all ten areas rather than by any numeric weighting [UNKNOWN: official FK-by-FK item percentages]

study-material domains under each FK area are paraphrases of the FK wording itself (the biomedical subject the FK denotes), not invented syllabi; specific commercial textbooks are not named because the research file did not verify any
the candidate is a non-CODA foreign graduate who reaches INBDE eligibility via ECE credential evaluation plus a DENTPIN, then sits the same INBDE as CODA candidates
exclusions: the full verbatim enumeration and official numbering of the 56 Clinical Content (CC) areas (proxy-blocked, held [UNKNOWN] and mapped to CC_AXIS_BLOCKER, never fabricated here)
the separate clinical/hands-on licensure exam (ADEX/DLOSCE/CDCA-WREB-CITA) and the state-by-state licensure map (a different specialist's scope; the INBDE is knowledge-only)
the education gate (CODA advanced-standing DDS/DMD via ADEA CAAPID) and credential-evaluation mechanics beyond naming ECE+DENTPIN as the FK-exam eligibility precondition
stating a fabricated per-FK item percentage, a fabricated 56-CC list, or an unverified current pass-rate/fee/retake number as fact
test-taking tactics, commercial question-bank quality judgments, and any endorsement of a specific prep vendor

glossary.definition: Integrated National Board Dental Examination — the single computer-based national board knowledge exam required across US licensing jurisdictions, launched August 2020 to replace NBDE Part I and Part II, run by the Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE) under the ADA. Knowledge-only: it does not satisfy the separate clinical exam. [FACT]

One of the two blueprint axes: ten biomedical/behavioral science areas (FK1-FK10) that every INBDE item draws on, applied within a clinical context. Enumerated in this KB as [ESTIMATE - high confidence] because the defining JCNDE PDFs were 403-blocked at compile time.

The other blueprint axis: 56 clinical-task areas grouped into three components (Diagnosis and Treatment Planning; Oral Health Management; Practice and Profession). The count of 56 is [FACT]; the full verbatim enumeration with official numbering is [UNKNOWN] here (proxy-blocked).

The JCNDE model that defines the INBDE blueprint as a 10 FK x 56 CC matrix; the Model Domain of Dentistry PDF and the July-2018 Domain of Dentistry are its authoritative artifacts (existence [FACT]; direct fetch 403 under egress policy).

The design principle that makes the exam 'Integrated': each scored item is written to apply at least one Foundation Knowledge area within a Clinical Content area, so FK is never tested as isolated recall but as biomedical reasoning inside a clinical task. [FACT]

The JCNDE document that defines the FK and CC areas (with Figures 1-4) and sample item construction; the primary source to verify the FK wording and the 56-CC list verbatim. Existence [FACT]; URL 403 under egress policy at compile time.

The honesty label for a claim reconstructed from official-page search snippets plus secondary corroboration but not confirmed against a directly-read official page — e.g. the FK1-FK10 wording, which is high-confidence but must be verified verbatim in the Item Development Guide.

The honesty label for a fact the research could not verify at all and must not invent — here the official per-FK item weights and the full verbatim 56-CC enumeration; each is carried as a named node/edge-case naming the blocker, not filled with a fabricated value.

The by-FK-and-by-CC remediation feedback JCNDE gives a failing candidate (passing candidates receive only pass/fail, no numeric score). It is the one official signal that lets a retake candidate re-weight study across FK areas. [FACT]

nodes.definition: Establish the structural fact that frames the whole FK map: the INBDE blueprint is a matrix of 10 Foundation Knowledge (FK) areas by 56 Clinical Content (CC) areas, and the INBDE is a knowledge-only national board exam run by JCNDE under the ADA (launched August 2020, replacing NBDE Part I and II) [FACT - confirmed across official-page snippets and JCNDE Item Development Guide references]. The FK axis is the biomedical/behavioral science a candidate brings; the CC axis is the clinical task it is applied within. This KB maps the FK axis; the CC axis is named but its full enumeration is held elsewhere as a blocker. The knowledge exam does not satisfy the separate clinical (hands-on) licensure exam most states also require.

included: the 10 FK x 56 CC matrix structure as a FACT
INBDE identity: JCNDE/ADA, knowledge-only, replaced NBDE I and II in Aug 2020
the FK-axis vs CC-axis split this KB is organized around
excluded: the per-FK study content
the separate clinical exam and licensure pathway

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a blueprint revision or a directly-read official confirmation changes the matrix frame

pros.claim: Anchoring on the two-axis matrix keeps every FK study decision tied to how items are actually built rather than to a flat topic list
pros.example: reading FK1 anatomy as something tested inside a diagnosis-and-treatment-planning case, not as standalone recall

nodes.definition: State the principle that gives the exam its name: every scored INBDE item integrates at least one Foundation Knowledge area applied within a Clinical Content area, so FK is tested as biomedical reasoning inside a clinical task, never as isolated recall [FACT]. Case sets on Day 2 present a single patient with charts, radiographs and photos and ask items that pull FK1-FK10 into a diagnosis or management decision. The study consequence is decisive: FK areas must be learned in their clinical application, not as a disconnected basic-science syllabus, and the study map must pair each FK area with the kinds of clinical tasks it feeds.

nodes.definition: Enumerate the ten Foundation Knowledge areas as reconstructed from the JCNDE Domain of Dentistry, corroborated across independent secondary sources (Penn Libraries, UOP Dugoni, dentalproguide) [ESTIMATE - high confidence; verify exact phrasing in the Item Development Guide]. FK1: molecular, biochemical, cellular and systems-level development, structure and function. FK2: physics and chemistry to explain normal biology and pathobiology. FK3: physics and chemistry to explain the characteristics and use of technologies and materials. FK4: principles of genetic, congenital and developmental diseases/conditions and their clinical features for patient risk. FK5: cellular and molecular bases of immune and non-immune host-defense mechanisms. FK6: general and disease-specific pathology to assess patient risk. FK7: the biology of microorganisms in physiology and pathology. FK8: pharmacology. FK9: behavioral sciences, ethics and jurisprudence. FK10: research methodology and analysis, and informatics tools. This list is the spine every per-FK study node hangs from.

included: all ten FK areas FK1-FK10 with their subject wording
the [ESTIMATE - high confidence] provenance tag on the enumeration
the role as the spine of the per-FK study nodes
excluded: the study-material detail under each area (per-FK nodes)
any per-FK item weighting

nodes.definition: Carry the [UNKNOWN] blocker that governs study-time allocation: JCNDE does not publish a public fixed per-FK item-weight table — items are distributed across the ten FK areas but no official FK-by-FK percentage is released [UNKNOWN: official FK-by-FK item percentages]. nodes.definition: Map FK1 — molecular, biochemical, cellular and systems-level development, structure and function — to its study content: gross anatomy with an emphasis on head-and-neck and oral anatomy, oral histology and dental/craniofacial embryology, tooth morphology, biochemistry (metabolism, macromolecules), and organ-system physiology. This is the broadest biomedical-foundation area and underpins normal-structure recognition that later FK areas build disease onto. Studied in application (per the integration principle), FK1 supports recognizing the normal range of structure and function against which clinical deviations are judged [FK1 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence; the subject domains it denotes are standard biomedical science].

included: head-and-neck/oral gross anatomy, oral histology and embryology, tooth morphology
biochemistry and organ-system physiology as the normal-structure foundation
excluded: disease/pathology overlays (FK4/FK6)
microbial and immune content (FK5/FK7)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a verbatim FK1 wording or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK1 map

pros.claim: Treating FK1 as the normal-structure foundation gives every later disease-and-risk FK area a baseline to deviate from
pros.example: learning normal pulpal and periodontal anatomy before studying their pathology in FK6

cons.claim: FK1 is broad, so an unbounded basic-science deep-dive can crowd out the clinically applied focus the exam rewards
cons.example: over-investing in biochemistry pathways with little dental-clinical yield

failure_modes: studying FK1 as encyclopedic basic science disconnected from clinical application
neglecting head-and-neck/oral anatomy in favor of general anatomy
acceptance_tests: FK1 is mapped to head-and-neck/oral anatomy, oral histology/embryology, tooth morphology, biochemistry and physiology, framed as the normal-structure foundation

nodes.definition: Map FK2 — physics and chemistry to explain normal biology and pathobiology — to its study content: the physical and chemical principles behind physiology and disease, such as acid-base and buffering (relevant to caries and saliva), fluid/electrolyte and osmotic behavior, thermodynamics and reaction kinetics in metabolism, and the chemistry of biomolecules and biological signaling. FK2 is the 'why the biology works' layer applied to normal and pathological function, and is distinct from FK3, which applies physics and chemistry to materials and technologies rather than to living tissue [FK2 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: physical/chemical principles behind normal and disease biology
acid-base/buffering, electrolytes, kinetics, biomolecular chemistry as applied to tissue
excluded: materials and device physics/chemistry (FK3)
the microbiology and immunology of disease (FK5/FK7)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sharpened FK2/FK3 boundary or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK2 map

pros.claim: Anchoring FK2 to biological explanation keeps it from being confused with the materials science of FK3
pros.example: studying saliva buffering and demineralization chemistry under FK2, not restorative-material chemistry

cons.claim: The FK2/FK3 boundary is subtle, so physics/chemistry content can be double-counted or misfiled between them
cons.example: filing bonding chemistry under FK2 when it is materials-and-technology FK3 content

failure_modes: conflating FK2 biological physics/chemistry with FK3 materials science
skipping FK2 as 'pre-dental chemistry' rather than applied pathobiology
acceptance_tests: FK2 is mapped to physics/chemistry explaining normal and disease biology and is explicitly separated from FK3 materials/technology
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK2/FK3 boundary
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK2 weakness
the FK2 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK3 — physics and chemistry to explain the characteristics and use of technologies and materials — to its study content: dental biomaterials science, including the composition, mechanical and physical properties, setting/curing reactions and clinical behavior of restoratives (composites, amalgam, glass ionomers), cements, impression materials, ceramics, metals/alloys, and the physics of imaging and dental instrumentation. FK3 is the materials-and-technology counterpart to FK2's biological physics/chemistry and must be studied distinctly — general chemistry (FK2) does not cover biomaterials selection and behavior [FK3 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: dental biomaterials composition, properties, setting reactions and clinical behavior
the physics of dental imaging and instrumentation
excluded: biological physics/chemistry of tissue (FK2)
the clinical restorative procedures themselves (Clinical Content, not FK)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sharpened FK2/FK3 boundary or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK3 map

pros.example: learning composite polymerization shrinkage and glass-ionomer fluoride release under FK3 explicitly

cons.claim: Biomaterials is a large distinct body of knowledge, so under-scoping FK3 to 'chemistry' leaves a real gap
cons.example: a candidate strong in general chemistry still missing amalgam/alloy and ceramic property items

failure_modes: assuming FK2 chemistry covers FK3 materials and skipping biomaterials

acceptance_tests: FK3 is mapped to dental biomaterials properties/behavior and imaging/instrumentation physics and is explicitly distinguished from FK2
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK2/FK3 boundary

nodes.definition: Map FK4 — principles of genetic, congenital and developmental diseases and conditions and their clinical features to understand patient risk — to its study content: basic and medical genetics, inheritance patterns, congenital and craniofacial developmental anomalies (e.g. cleft lip/palate, amelogenesis/dentinogenesis imperfecta), and how their clinical features raise or modify patient risk. FK4 is framed explicitly as a patient-risk lens: the point is recognizing conditions that change management, not genetics for its own sake. It sits alongside FK6 (general/acquired pathology) with FK4 owning the developmental/heritable origin [FK4 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: genetics, inheritance, congenital and craniofacial developmental anomalies
their clinical features as a patient-risk lens
excluded: acquired/general pathology (FK6)
the clinical management tasks themselves (Clinical Content)

pros.claim: Framing FK4 as patient-risk keeps genetics clinically relevant and connected to management decisions
pros.example: recognizing a developmental enamel defect as a risk/management modifier rather than a trivia item

cons.claim: Developmental and general pathology overlap, so FK4 and FK6 content can blur without a clear origin boundary
cons.example: filing an acquired condition under FK4's developmental scope

failure_modes: studying genetics abstractly instead of as clinical patient-risk features

acceptance_tests: FK4 is mapped to genetic/congenital/developmental conditions and their clinical features as a patient-risk lens, distinct from FK6
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK4/FK6 boundary

the FK4 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK5 — cellular and molecular bases of immune and non-immune host-defense mechanisms — to its study content: innate and adaptive immunology, inflammation, hypersensitivity and autoimmunity, and non-immune barrier/defense mechanisms relevant to oral and systemic health (e.g. mucosal defense, salivary protective factors). FK5 is the host side of the host-pathogen interface it shares with FK7 (microbiology): FK5 owns the defense response, FK7 owns the organisms. Studied in application it supports understanding periodontal and mucosal disease immunopathology and patient susceptibility [FK5 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: innate/adaptive immunology, inflammation, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity
non-immune barrier/host-defense mechanisms including oral protective factors
excluded: the microorganisms themselves (FK7)
systemic pharmacotherapy of immune disease (FK8)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sharpened FK5/FK7 boundary or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK5 map

pros.claim: Treating FK5 as the host-defense half of the interface keeps immunology paired with, not merged into, microbiology
pros.example: studying periodontal immunopathology under FK5 and the periodontal microbiome under FK7

cons.claim: Immunology and microbiology interlock, so a candidate may study one and assume the other is covered
cons.example: learning host inflammatory response but neglecting the microbial trigger in FK7

failure_modes: merging FK5 immunology into FK7 microbiology and under-studying host defense
treating immunology as pure basic science disconnected from oral disease
acceptance_tests: FK5 is mapped to immune and non-immune host-defense mechanisms and paired with FK7 across the host-pathogen interface
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK5/FK7 boundary
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK5 weakness
the FK5 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK6 — general and disease-specific pathology to assess patient risk — to its study content: general pathology mechanisms (cell injury, inflammation, neoplasia), systemic disease relevant to dental care (cardiovascular, endocrine/diabetes, bleeding disorders, immunosuppression), and oral and maxillofacial pathology of the hard and soft tissues. FK6 is the acquired-disease counterpart to FK4's developmental origin and is framed as patient-risk assessment: the clinical point is medical-history-driven risk stratification and oral-lesion recognition, not pathology in the abstract [FK6 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: general pathology mechanisms, dentally relevant systemic disease, oral/maxillofacial pathology
patient-risk stratification and lesion recognition
excluded: developmental/genetic origin conditions (FK4)
the pharmacologic management of disease (FK8)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sharpened FK4/FK6 boundary or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK6 map

pros.claim: Framing FK6 as patient-risk assessment ties pathology directly to medical-history-driven clinical safety
pros.example: recognizing how uncontrolled diabetes or a bleeding disorder modifies dental risk and management

cons.claim: FK6 is large and overlaps FK4 and FK5, so scope can sprawl without the acquired-disease/patient-risk boundary
cons.example: re-studying immunology already owned by FK5 under FK6's inflammation heading

failure_modes: studying pathology abstractly rather than as patient-risk
blurring FK6 acquired disease with FK4 developmental conditions
acceptance_tests: FK6 is mapped to general/systemic/oral pathology as a patient-risk assessment, distinct from FK4 developmental origin
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK4/FK6 boundary
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK6 weakness
the FK6 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK7 — the biology of microorganisms in physiology and pathology — to its study content: general and oral microbiology, bacteria/viruses/fungi relevant to health and disease, the oral microbiome and biofilm/plaque ecology, cariogenic and periodontal pathogens, and clinically relevant infectious diseases and their transmission (informing infection control). FK7 is the pathogen half of the interface it shares with FK5 (host defense) and connects forward to FK8 antimicrobial pharmacology. Studied in application it supports understanding caries and periodontal disease etiology and cross-infection control [FK7 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: general/oral microbiology, the oral microbiome and biofilm ecology, cariogenic/periodontal pathogens
clinically relevant infectious diseases and transmission
excluded: the host immune response (FK5)
antimicrobial drug pharmacology (FK8)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sharpened FK5/FK7/FK8 boundary or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK7 map

pros.claim: Treating FK7 as the pathogen half keeps microbiology paired with host defense and linked to antimicrobial therapy
pros.example: connecting periodontal pathogens (FK7) to host immunopathology (FK5) and to antibiotic choice (FK8)

cons.claim: Microbiology interlocks with immunology and pharmacology, so its boundaries with FK5 and FK8 can blur
cons.example: studying antibiotic spectrum under FK7 when drug pharmacology is FK8

failure_modes: merging FK7 microbiology into FK5 immunology
neglecting oral-microbiome/biofilm ecology in favor of general microbiology
acceptance_tests: FK7 is mapped to the biology of microorganisms including the oral microbiome and pathogens, paired with FK5 and linked forward to FK8
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide sharpens the FK5/FK7/FK8 boundaries
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK7 weakness
the FK7 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK8 — pharmacology — to its study content: general pharmacological principles (pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics), the major drug classes and their mechanisms, dental therapeutics (local anesthetics, analgesics including opioids and NSAIDs, antibiotics and antimicrobials, sedatives/anxiolytics), adverse drug effects and drug-drug/drug-disease interactions, and prescribing considerations for medically complex and special-population patients. FK8 connects to FK7 (antimicrobial targets) and to the Oral Health Management clinical tasks of selecting, prescribing and managing complications of pharmacological agents. It is a high-yield, high-safety-consequence area [FK8 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: pharmacokinetics/dynamics, drug classes and mechanisms, dental therapeutics
adverse effects, interactions and prescribing for medically complex patients
excluded: the microorganisms antimicrobials target (FK7)
the clinical procedural administration tasks (Clinical Content)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a clarified FK8 scope or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK8 map

pros.claim: A structured FK8 map covers a high-yield, high-safety area that recurs across integrated management items
pros.example: mastering local-anesthetic and analgesic selection and interactions that appear in patient-case items

cons.claim: Pharmacology is broad and detail-dense, so unfocused memorization can consume time better spent on integrated application
cons.example: memorizing exhaustive drug tables without the interaction/complication reasoning items test

failure_modes: studying drug lists in isolation rather than as prescribing/interaction reasoning
neglecting drug-disease interactions for medically complex patients
acceptance_tests: FK8 is mapped to pharmacokinetics/dynamics, dental drug classes/therapeutics, adverse effects/interactions and complex-patient prescribing
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide clarifies FK8 scope
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK8 weakness
the FK8 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK9 — behavioral sciences, ethics and jurisprudence — to its study content: behavioral science and patient communication (behavior management, health behavior, pain/anxiety behavior), professional ethics and the core ethical principles, informed consent, and dental jurisprudence (record-keeping, scope of practice, regulatory obligations such as HIPAA/OSHA). FK9 is a full science area, not a soft add-on: it is the foundation the Practice-and-Profession Clinical Content group leans on most heavily, and foreign-trained candidates often under-prepare it because it is jurisdiction-specific. It must be studied to competence like any biomedical area [FK9 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: behavioral science and patient communication, professional ethics and informed consent, dental jurisprudence and regulatory obligations
excluded: the clinical practice-management tasks themselves (Clinical Content)
the research-ethics/statistics content of FK10

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a clarified FK9 scope or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK9 map

pros.claim: Treating FK9 as a full area corrects the common under-preparation of behavioral/ethics/legal content by foreign-trained candidates
pros.example: studying US informed-consent and jurisprudence norms rather than assuming a home-jurisdiction equivalent

cons.claim: Jurisprudence is jurisdiction-specific and partly overlaps state-licensure rules outside the exam's scope, so scope must be kept to the exam's ethics/law
cons.example: over-studying one state's statutes rather than the exam-level ethics and jurisprudence principles

failure_modes: dismissing FK9 as non-science and under-studying it
confusing exam-level jurisprudence with state-specific licensure law
acceptance_tests: FK9 is mapped to behavioral science, professional ethics/informed consent and dental jurisprudence and linked to the Practice-and-Profession CC group
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide clarifies FK9 scope
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK9 weakness
the FK9 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Map FK10 — research methodology and analysis, and informatics tools — to its study content: study design and levels of evidence, biostatistics and critical appraisal of the literature, epidemiology basics, evidence-based dentistry, and health-informatics tools that support patient care and practice. FK10 underpins the evidence-based reasoning that integrated items expect (e.g. interpreting a study or a diagnostic-test statistic) and is the most easily neglected area because it is not clinically 'hands-on.' It must be studied to competence, especially critical-appraisal and basic biostatistics [FK10 wording ESTIMATE - high confidence].

included: study design/levels of evidence, biostatistics and critical appraisal, epidemiology, evidence-based dentistry, health informatics tools
excluded: research ethics owned by FK9's professional ethics
the clinical procedures the evidence informs (Clinical Content)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a clarified FK10 scope or a diagnostic-feedback weakness updates the FK10 map

pros.claim: A dedicated FK10 map protects an easily neglected area that integrated evidence-interpretation items reward
pros.example: practicing critical appraisal and biostatistics so a study-interpretation item is answerable

cons.claim: FK10 feels abstract and low-yield to clinically-minded candidates, so it competes poorly for study time without a deliberate allocation
cons.example: skipping biostatistics as 'not real dentistry' and missing evidence-appraisal items

failure_modes: neglecting FK10 as non-clinical and losing evidence-appraisal items
confusing FK10 research methodology with FK9 professional/research ethics
acceptance_tests: FK10 is mapped to study design, biostatistics/critical appraisal, epidemiology, evidence-based dentistry and informatics tools
revisit_triggers: the Item Development Guide clarifies FK10 scope
a diagnostic-feedback report flags FK10 weakness
the FK10 wording is corrected on verbatim verification

nodes.definition: Compose the material map the KB is built to produce: each of the ten FK areas paired with what to study and which authoritative artifact defines it, allocated for full coverage rather than by any per-FK weight (which does not exist [UNKNOWN]). The map studies every FK area to competence, learns each in clinical application within the CC axis (integration principle), verifies wording against the Item Development Guide where fetch access exists, and treats secondary aggregators as corroboration only. Because no official weighting is available, deepening is driven by personal diagnostic feedback, not a published number. The map is the actionable synthesis handed to a candidate.

included: the ten-area FK-to-study-content-and-source pairing
the coverage-based (not weight-based) allocation and integrated-application study rule
the verify-against-official-source rule
excluded: the retake diagnostic-feedback re-weighting (its own node)
the final go/no-go readiness synthesis (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an official weight table, a diagnostic-feedback re-weighting, or a verbatim verification updates the map

pros.claim: A single integrated map keeps all ten FK areas covered and sourced instead of an uneven ad hoc topic list
pros.example: handing a candidate one sheet pairing FK1-FK10 with study content and the Item Development Guide as source

cons.claim: Coverage-based allocation without weights gives coarse time-budgeting, so the map cannot tell a candidate exactly where to spend most
cons.example: a time-pressed candidate wanting a ranked FK priority the absent weights cannot supply

failure_modes: allocating study by an invented per-FK weight instead of coverage
studying FK areas in isolation rather than integrated within CC
acceptance_tests: the map pairs all ten FK areas with study content and an authoritative source, allocates by full coverage with no invented weight, and mandates integrated-within-CC study
revisit_triggers: an official per-FK weight table is published and enables ranked allocation
a diagnostic-feedback report re-weights a candidate's emphasis
the FK wording or CC list is verified verbatim

nodes.definition: Wire in the one official personalization signal: JCNDE reports results as pass/fail, and a failing candidate receives diagnostic performance feedback broken down by FK and CC areas, while passing candidates receive no numeric score [FACT]. Because no public per-FK weight exists, this diagnostic feedback is the only official basis for re-weighting study on a retake — it substitutes personal weakness data for the missing weighting table. The rule: a first attempt is planned by full coverage; a retake is re-weighted toward the FK/CC areas the diagnostic report flags, without inferring official weights from one candidate's report. Passing candidates get no such signal, so their prep must be coverage-complete the first time.

included: the pass/fail reporting and by-FK/by-CC diagnostic feedback for failers [FACT]
using that feedback as the retake re-weighting signal in place of absent weights
the caution against inferring official weights from one report
excluded: the official per-FK weight blocker itself (its own node)
the exam pass standard mechanics beyond the reporting model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reporting-model change or an official weight table updates the feedback loop

pros.claim: Using the official diagnostic feedback gives a retake candidate a legitimate, personalized basis to re-weight study
pros.example: a failer with flagged FK8 and FK10 areas deepening those instead of re-studying uniformly

cons.claim: The signal only exists after a failed attempt, so it cannot guide a first attempt and passers get nothing
cons.example: a first-time candidate having no diagnostic data and needing full coverage regardless

failure_modes: ignoring the FK/CC diagnostic report and re-studying uniformly on a retake
over-generalizing one candidate's feedback into an inferred official weighting
acceptance_tests: the loop states pass/fail reporting with by-FK/by-CC diagnostic feedback for failers, uses it as the retake re-weighting signal, and warns against inferring official weights from it
revisit_triggers: JCNDE changes the score-reporting or diagnostic-feedback model
an official per-FK weight table removes the need for feedback-based re-weighting
a candidate's diagnostic report is received

nodes.definition: Compose the KB's terminal synthesis: a defensible FK study plan is ready when it covers all ten FK areas to competence (integrated within the CC axis), sources each against the authoritative JCNDE artifacts, allocates time by coverage and personal diagnostic feedback rather than any invented weight, and explicitly carries its two blockers — no official per-FK weights and no verified full 56-CC list — as named verification follow-ups rather than fabricated content. Reconciled rules: never publish a per-FK percentage or a complete 56-CC list without verbatim verification; study FK in application, not in isolation; verify the reconstructed FK wording against the Item Development Guide when fetch access exists. A plan that is coverage-complete but hides its blockers is not defensible; a plan that names them is.

included: the ready-when conditions: all-ten coverage, sourced, coverage/feedback-allocated, blockers named
the reconciled never-fabricate and study-in-application rules
the defensible-plan-names-its-blockers conclusion
excluded: the per-FK study detail (the FK-area nodes)
the separate clinical exam and licensure readiness

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a lifted blocker, a diagnostic re-weighting, or a blueprint revision updates the plan synthesis

pros.claim: A single readiness synthesis prevents shipping a study plan that looks complete but hides its [UNKNOWN] blockers
pros.example: declaring a plan defensible only once the missing weights and CC list are carried as named follow-ups, not invented

cons.claim: A blocker-honest plan is less tidy than one that pretends to full official weighting and enumeration a candidate might prefer
cons.example: a candidate wanting a ranked per-FK plan the honest synthesis declines to fabricate

failure_modes: declaring the plan ready while a fabricated weight or CC list hides a blocker
dropping the integrated-application rule and reverting to siloed basic-science study
acceptance_tests: the synthesis conditions readiness on all-ten coverage, authoritative sourcing, coverage/feedback allocation and both named blockers, and refuses any fabricated per-FK weight or complete 56-CC list
revisit_triggers: either blocker is lifted by verbatim verification
a diagnostic-feedback report or an official weight table changes allocation
JCNDE revises the FK/CC blueprint

conflict_axes.name: invented_weight_vs_coverage_allocation
conflict_axes.description: The absent official per-FK item weighting tempts a plausible-but-fabricated per-FK ranking, while the honest allocation is full coverage of all ten areas.
poles: allocate by an invented per-FK weight
allocate by full coverage and diagnostic feedback
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: study all ten areas to competence and deepen by personal diagnostic feedback, publishing no per-FK percentage until an official table exists

conflict_axes.name: verified_estimate_vs_official_verbatim
conflict_axes.description: The FK wording is high-confidence [ESTIMATE] reconstructed from blocked official pages, pulling against waiting for verbatim official confirmation before use.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the enumeration for study but keep the [ESTIMATE] tag and verify against the Item Development Guide when fetch access exists

conflict_axes.name: fk_silo_study_vs_integrated_application
conflict_axes.description: Studying FK areas as isolated basic science is simpler than learning each in its integrated clinical application, which the exam actually rewards.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: learn each FK area paired with the clinical tasks it feeds, per the integration principle, not as a disconnected syllabus

conflict_axes.name: cc_axis_gap_vs_fk_focus
conflict_axes.description: This KB maps the FK axis, but items live in the CC axis whose full list is blocked, risking either ignoring CC or fabricating it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the CC gap as a named [UNKNOWN] follow-up, use the verified CC themes and counts, and pair FK with CC only where verified

conflict_axes.name: breadth_across_ten_vs_depth_in_weak
conflict_axes.description: Covering all ten FK areas competes for time with going deep in a candidate's weak areas, with no official weight to arbitrate.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: guarantee competence coverage of all ten first, then deepen where diagnostic feedback (not a published weight) shows weakness

conflict_axes.name: basic_science_recall_vs_clinical_reasoning
conflict_axes.description: FK content can be learned as basic-science recall or as integrated clinical reasoning, and the integrated items reward the latter.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: anchor FK study in patient-case reasoning so recall serves diagnosis and management, not standalone facts

conflict_axes.name: official_403_vs_secondary_aggregators
conflict_axes.description: The defining official artifacts were 403-blocked, so the map leans on secondary aggregators that must not be treated as authoritative.
poles: hold official artifacts as source of truth
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use secondary aggregators only as corroboration and verify FK/CC wording against the official Item Development Guide when reachable

conflict_axes.name: physchem_biology_vs_materials_conflation
conflict_axes.description: FK2 (physics/chemistry for biology) and FK3 (physics/chemistry for materials) share methods and are easily double-counted or conflated.
poles: merge FK2 and FK3 as chemistry
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: file biological explanation under FK2 and biomaterials/technology under FK3, and do not assume general chemistry covers biomaterials

conflict_axes.name: remediation_feedback_vs_proactive_coverage
conflict_axes.description: Retake re-weighting from diagnostic feedback pulls against the need for coverage-complete preparation on a first attempt that yields no such signal.
poles: wait for diagnostic feedback to prioritize
cover all areas proactively first time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prepare coverage-complete for the first attempt and reserve diagnostic-feedback re-weighting for retakes, since passers get no feedback

dominance_rules.action: verify it against the live Candidate Guide and Apply page before relying on it and keep the [ESTIMATE] tag until then

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag the FK enumeration [ESTIMATE - high confidence] the first time it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a reconstructed FK wording later being quoted as verbatim-official and retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the full 56-CC enumeration as [UNKNOWN] up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream KB shipping a fabricated complete official CC list that must be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Allocate study by coverage from the start, never build a per-FK weighting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented per-FK percentage steering study and being corrected after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the official artifact URLs even while they are 403 under egress
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fetch-enabled run having to re-research the FK/CC wording from scratch to verify it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Study each FK area integrated within CC application from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-learning siloed basic science as clinical reasoning after failing integrated items

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate FK2 (biology physics/chemistry) and FK3 (materials science) in the map from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-mapping biomaterials content mistakenly assumed covered by general chemistry

anti_rework_rules.rule: Wire the diagnostic-feedback loop into the plan before the first attempt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a retake being planned uniformly because no re-weighting mechanism was designed in

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify fees, retake interval and format against the live Candidate Guide before relying on them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: acting on [ESTIMATE] secondary numbers that a live guide later contradicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fetch-enabled run reads the Item Development Guide PDF directly
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [ESTIMATE] FK wording with the verbatim text and re-tag it toward [FACT]

iteration_protocol.trigger: the full 56 Clinical Content areas are extracted verbatim with official numbering
iteration_protocol.action: replace the CC blocker with the verified list and re-derive precise FK-to-CC integration pairing

iteration_protocol.trigger: JCNDE publishes an official per-FK (or per-CC) item-weight table
iteration_protocol.action: lift the weight blocker and re-allocate study time by the published weighting

iteration_protocol.trigger: a candidate's by-FK/by-CC diagnostic feedback report is received
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight the retake study emphasis toward the flagged FK areas

iteration_protocol.trigger: the live Candidate Guide confirms the fee, retake interval or format
iteration_protocol.action: update the honesty tags on those secondary facts and remove the [ESTIMATE] flag where verified

iteration_protocol.trigger: JCNDE issues a revised blueprint or a new FK area definition
iteration_protocol.action: re-frame the matrix and re-enumerate the FK areas

iteration_protocol.trigger: a free official JCNDE practice test is confirmed to exist separate from the guide
iteration_protocol.action: add it to the authoritative source map and the study material map
